records.literal_gloss: And will be dismayed your mighty men, Teman, so that will be cut off everyone from [the] mountain of Esau by slaughter.

en.L: And your mighty men will be shattered, Teman, \q so that everyone will be cut off from Mount Esau by slaughter.
en.B: Your warriors will be terrified, Teman, \q so that everyone on Mount Esau will be cut down in the slaughter.
en.R: Your soldiers, Teman, will be terrified, \q and everyone on Mount Esau will be killed.

es.L: Y tus valientes serán quebrantados, oh Temán, \q para que todo hombre sea cortado del monte de Esaú por la matanza.
es.B: Tus guerreros, Temán, quedarán aterrados, \q y todos en el monte de Esaú caerán en la matanza.
es.R: Tus soldados, Temán, estarán aterrados, \q y todos los que viven en el monte de Esaú morirán.

fr.L: Et tes héros seront brisés, Téman, \q afin que tout homme soit retranché de la montagne d’Ésaü par le massacre.
fr.B: Tes guerriers, Téman, seront terrifiés, \q et tous ceux de la montagne d’Ésaü tomberont dans le massacre.
fr.R: Tes soldats, Téman, seront terrifiés, \q et tous ceux de la montagne d’Ésaü seront tués.

sw.L: Na mashujaa wako watavunjika moyo, ee Temani, \q ili kila mtu akatiliwe mbali kutoka mlima wa Esau kwa machinjo.
sw.B: Mashujaa wako, ee Temani, watatishika, \q hata kila mtu katika mlima wa Esau atakatiliwa mbali katika machinjo.
sw.R: Askari wako, ee Temani, wataogopa sana, \q na kila mtu katika mlima wa Esau atauawa.

vi.L: Và các dũng sĩ của ngươi sẽ bị tan vỡ, hỡi Thê-man, \q để mọi người bị diệt khỏi núi Ê-sau bởi cuộc tàn sát.
vi.B: Hỡi Thê-man, các chiến binh của ngươi sẽ kinh hoàng, \q và mọi người trên núi Ê-sau sẽ bị giết trong cuộc tàn sát.
vi.R: Hỡi Thê-man, quân lính của ngươi sẽ kinh hãi, \q và mọi người trên núi Ê-sau sẽ bị giết.

ko.L: 데만아, 네 용사들이 꺾일 것이니, \q 에서의 산에서 모든 사람이 살육으로 끊어질 것이다.
ko.B: 데만아, 네 용사들이 공포에 질릴 것이니, \q 에서의 산에 있는 사람은 모두 살육을 당하여 쓰러질 것이다.
ko.R: 데만아, 네 군인들이 겁에 질릴 것이다. \q 에서의 산에 사는 사람은 모두 죽임을 당할 것이다.

decisions.choice: Teman: one of Edom's chief regions, standing for the whole land
decisions.reason: Teman was a region, and perhaps a town, in the south of Edom, named after a grandson of Esau (Genesis 36:11). As in Jeremiah 49:7 and 20, it stands for Edom as a whole, beside Mount Esau.

decisions.choice: by slaughter: the last words of verse 9
alternatives: the first words of verse 10: "because of the slaughter, because of the violence done to your brother Jacob"
decisions.reason: The verse division and the accents of the Hebrew text place "by slaughter" at the end of verse 9. Some ancient translations, among them the Greek and the Latin, join it to verse 10, so that Edom is judged "because of the slaughter" of its brother. The Hebrew division is followed. This description of the ancient translations is written from general knowledge.

decisions.choice: dismayed: shattered with terror
decisions.reason: The verb means to be broken, and so to be broken in spirit, terrified (Jeremiah 49:37). The warriors lose their nerve, and the people are left without defense.

decisions.choice: shattered (L); terrified (B, R); cut down ... killed (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the picture of breaking; Balanced and Readable give its sense here, terror. "Everyone" is the Hebrew "each man"; the sense is everyone left on Mount Esau. Readable says "killed" for "cut off by slaughter".

source.text: מֵחֲמַ֛ס אָחִ֥יךָ יַעֲקֹ֖ב תְּכַסְּךָ֣ בוּשָׁ֑ה וְנִכְרַ֖תָּ לְעוֹלָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: Because of [the] violence [to] your brother Jacob, shame will cover you, and you will be cut off forever.

en.L: Because of the violence [done to] your brother Jacob, disgrace will cover you, \q and you will be cut off for all time.
en.B: Because of the violence you did to your brother Jacob, \q you will be covered in shame and cut off forever.
en.R: You were cruel to your brother Jacob's people, so you will be covered with shame, \q and you will be destroyed forever.

es.L: Por la violencia [hecha] a tu hermano Jacob, te cubrirá la vergüenza, \q y serás cortado para siempre.
es.B: Por la violencia que hiciste a tu hermano Jacob, \q te cubrirá la vergüenza y serás exterminado para siempre.
es.R: Fuiste cruel con el pueblo de tu hermano Jacob, por eso te cubrirá la vergüenza, \q y serás destruido para siempre.

fr.L: À cause de la violence [faite] à ton frère Jacob, la honte te couvrira, \q et tu seras retranché pour toujours.
fr.B: À cause de la violence que tu as faite à ton frère Jacob, \q tu seras couvert de honte et retranché pour toujours.
fr.R: Tu as été cruel envers le peuple de ton frère Jacob, alors tu seras couvert de honte, \q et tu seras détruit pour toujours.

sw.L: Kwa sababu ya udhalimu [uliomtendea] ndugu yako Yakobo, aibu itakufunika, \q nawe utakatiliwa mbali milele.
sw.B: Kwa sababu ya ukatili uliomtendea ndugu yako Yakobo, \q utafunikwa na aibu na kukatiliwa mbali milele.
sw.R: Uliwatendea ukatili watu wa ndugu yako Yakobo, kwa hiyo utafunikwa na aibu, \q nawe utaangamizwa milele.

vi.L: Vì sự bạo ngược [đối với] anh em ngươi là Gia-cốp, sự sỉ nhục sẽ bao phủ ngươi, \q và ngươi sẽ bị diệt đến đời đời.
vi.B: Vì sự bạo ngược ngươi đã làm cho anh em ngươi là Gia-cốp, \q ngươi sẽ bị hổ thẹn bao phủ và bị diệt mãi mãi.
vi.R: Ngươi đã đối xử tàn ác với dân của anh em ngươi là Gia-cốp, nên ngươi sẽ bị hổ thẹn bao phủ, \q và ngươi sẽ bị tiêu diệt đời đời.

ko.L: 네 형제 야곱에게 [저지른] 폭력 때문에 수치가 너를 덮을 것이고, \q 너는 영원히 끊어질 것이다.
ko.B: 네가 네 형제 야곱에게 휘두른 폭력 때문에 \q 너는 수치를 뒤집어쓰고 영원히 끊어질 것이다.
ko.R: 너는 네 형제 야곱의 자손에게 잔인하게 굴었다. 그러므로 너는 수치를 뒤집어쓰고, \q 영원히 멸망할 것이다.

decisions.choice: your brother Jacob: the charge is that Edom wronged its own brother
decisions.reason: Esau and Jacob were twins (Genesis 25:24-26), and the law reminded Israel that "the Edomite is your brother" (Deuteronomy 23:8; compare Numbers 20:14). Edom's guilt is the greater because the violence was done to its own kin. Here the verses turn from Edom's pride to the reason for its judgment, set out in verses 11-14.

decisions.choice: violence: wrong done by force, cruelty
decisions.reason: The word means violent wrongdoing, the cruelty that breaks the bonds between people (Genesis 6:11; Joel 4:19, where it is again used of Edom's violence against Judah).

decisions.choice: [done to] (L); you did to (B); You were cruel to your brother Jacob's people (R); disgrace (L); shame (B, R)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says only "the violence of your brother", meaning the violence done to him. Literal brackets the words that say so; Balanced and Readable state them. Readable says "Jacob's people" because Jacob here stands for the nation descended from him, and "destroyed" for "cut off". Literal says "disgrace" and "for all time", Balanced and Readable "shame" and "forever"; the words mean the same.

source.text: בְּיוֹם֙ עֲמָֽדְךָ֣ מִנֶּ֔גֶד בְּי֛וֹם שְׁב֥וֹת זָרִ֖ים חֵיל֑וֹ וְנָכְרִ֞ים בָּ֣אוּ שְׁעָרָ֗יו וְעַל־יְרוּשָׁלִַ֨ם֙ יַדּ֣וּ גוֹרָ֔ל גַּם־אַתָּ֖ה כְּאַחַ֥ד מֵהֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: On [the] day you stood aloof, on [the] day strangers carried off his wealth, and foreigners entered his gates, and for Jerusalem they cast lots, also you [were] like one of them.

en.L: On the day you stood aloof, \q on the day strangers carried off his wealth, \q and foreigners entered his gates and cast lots for Jerusalem, \q you too [were] like one of them.
en.B: On the day you stood at a distance, \q on the day strangers carried off his wealth \q and foreigners entered his gates and cast lots for Jerusalem, \q you were like one of them.
en.R: You stood by and watched \q when strangers carried off your brother's wealth. \q Foreigners came through his gates and threw lots to divide up Jerusalem. \q You were just like them!

es.L: El día en que te mantuviste aparte, \q el día en que extraños se llevaron su riqueza, \q y extranjeros entraron por sus puertas y echaron suertes sobre Jerusalén, \q también tú [eras] como uno de ellos.
es.B: El día en que te quedaste a distancia, \q el día en que extraños se llevaron su riqueza \q y extranjeros entraron por sus puertas y echaron suertes sobre Jerusalén, \q tú eras como uno de ellos.
es.R: Te quedaste mirando \q cuando unos extraños se llevaron la riqueza de tu hermano. \q Unos extranjeros entraron por sus puertas y echaron suertes para repartirse Jerusalén. \q ¡Tú eras igual que ellos!

fr.L: Le jour où tu t’es tenu à l’écart, \q le jour où des étrangers ont emporté ses richesses, \q et où des gens d’ailleurs sont entrés par ses portes et ont tiré Jérusalem au sort, \q toi aussi, tu [étais] comme l’un d’eux.
fr.B: Le jour où tu es resté à distance, \q le jour où des étrangers ont emporté ses richesses \q et où des gens d’ailleurs sont entrés par ses portes et ont tiré Jérusalem au sort, \q tu étais comme l’un d’eux.
fr.R: Tu es resté là à regarder \q quand des étrangers ont emporté les richesses de ton frère. \q Des gens d’ailleurs sont entrés par ses portes et ont tiré au sort pour se partager Jérusalem. \q Tu étais exactement comme eux !

sw.L: Siku ile uliposimama mbali, \q siku ile wageni walipochukua mali zake, \q na watu wa kigeni walipoingia malango yake na kupiga kura juu ya Yerusalemu, \q wewe pia [ulikuwa] kama mmoja wao.
sw.B: Siku ile uliposimama kwa mbali, \q siku ile wageni walipochukua mali zake \q na watu wa kigeni walipoingia malango yake na kupiga kura juu ya Yerusalemu, \q wewe ulikuwa kama mmoja wao.
sw.R: Ulisimama ukitazama tu \q wakati wageni walipochukua mali za ndugu yako. \q Watu wa kigeni waliingia kupitia malango yake na kupiga kura ili kugawana Yerusalemu. \q Wewe ulikuwa kama wao kabisa!

vi.L: Trong ngày ngươi đứng xa xa, \q trong ngày người lạ cướp đi của cải nó, \q và người ngoại bang vào các cổng nó và bắt thăm chia Giê-ru-sa-lem, \q ngươi cũng [như] một kẻ trong bọn chúng.
vi.B: Vào ngày ngươi đứng từ xa mà nhìn, \q vào ngày người lạ cướp đi của cải nó \q và người ngoại bang vào các cổng nó, bắt thăm chia Giê-ru-sa-lem, \q ngươi cũng như một kẻ trong bọn chúng.
vi.R: Ngươi đứng đó mà nhìn \q khi người lạ cướp đi của cải của anh em ngươi. \q Người ngoại bang vào qua các cổng thành và bắt thăm để chia nhau Giê-ru-sa-lem. \q Ngươi cũng chẳng khác gì chúng!

ko.L: 네가 멀리 서 있던 날, \q 낯선 자들이 그의 재물을 빼앗아 가던 날, \q 이방인들이 그의 성문에 들어가 예루살렘을 두고 제비를 뽑던 날, \q 너도 그들 가운데 하나와 같[았다].
ko.B: 네가 멀찍이 서 있던 날, \q 낯선 자들이 그의 재물을 빼앗아 가고 \q 이방인들이 그의 성문에 들어가 예루살렘을 두고 제비를 뽑던 날, \q 너는 그들 가운데 하나와 같았다.
ko.R: 너는 구경만 하고 서 있었다. \q 낯선 자들이 네 형제의 재물을 빼앗아 갈 때였다. \q 이방인들이 그의 성문으로 들어와 제비를 뽑아 예루살렘을 나누어 가졌다. \q 너도 그들과 똑같았다!

decisions.choice: the day strangers entered Jerusalem: the fall of the city, usually taken to be the Babylonian conquest of 586 BC
alternatives: an earlier attack on Jerusalem, such as that of the Philistines and Arabians in the days of Jehoram (2 Chronicles 21:16-17)
decisions.reason: The verse does not name the enemy. Psalm 137:7 remembers the Edomites crying "Tear it down!" on the day Jerusalem fell to Babylon, and Lamentations 4:21-22 and Ezekiel 35:5, 10-15 also accuse Edom over that disaster. That is the usual identification. Jerusalem was attacked more than once, and the description fits other attacks too.

decisions.choice: his wealth: Jacob's goods, or his army
alternatives: his army, carried off into captivity
decisions.reason: The word means strength, and so either wealth or a fighting force. The verb means to take captive. Carrying off goods fits verse 13, where Edom reaches for Jacob's wealth; but the line can also mean that strangers took his army captive.

decisions.choice: cast lots for Jerusalem: divided the city and its people as plunder
decisions.reason: Victors cast lots to share out captured people and goods (Joel 4:3; Nahum 3:10; Psalm 22:19). Edom took no part in the fighting, but by standing by it was like one of the conquerors.

decisions.choice: stood aloof (L); stood at a distance (B); stood by and watched (R)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says that Edom stood "from opposite", at a distance, as an onlooker who will not help. Readable says what that meant. Readable names "your brother" for "his", so the reader can follow who is meant, and says "threw lots to divide up" for casting lots (m3).

source.text: וְאַל־תֵּ֤רֶא בְיוֹם־אָחִ֨יךָ֙ בְּי֣וֹם נָכְר֔וֹ וְאַל־תִּשְׂמַ֥ח לִבְנֵֽי־יְהוּדָ֖ה בְּי֣וֹם אָבְדָ֑ם וְאַל־תַּגְדֵּ֥ל פִּ֖יךָ בְּי֥וֹם צָרָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And do not look on [the] day of your brother, on [the] day of his misfortune; and do not rejoice over [the] sons of Judah on [the] day of their perishing; and do not make big your mouth on [the] day of distress.

en.L: But do not look on the day of your brother, on the day of his misfortune; \q do not rejoice over the {{gender:children|sons}} of Judah on the day of their ruin; \q do not make your mouth big on the day of distress.
en.B: You should not have gloated over your brother's day, the day of his misfortune, \q nor rejoiced over the people of Judah on the day of their ruin, \q nor boasted so loudly on the day of their distress.
en.R: You should not have enjoyed watching your brother on the day his trouble came. \q You should not have been glad when the people of Judah were destroyed. \q You should not have bragged on the day they were in distress.

es.L: Pero no mires el día de tu hermano, el día de su desgracia; \q no te alegres por los hijos de Judá el día de su ruina; \q no agrandes tu boca el día de la angustia.
es.B: No debiste mirar con gozo el día de tu hermano, el día de su desgracia, \q ni alegrarte por la gente de Judá el día de su ruina, \q ni jactarte tanto el día de su angustia.
es.R: No debiste disfrutar viendo a tu hermano el día en que le llegó la desgracia. \q No debiste alegrarte cuando la gente de Judá fue destruida. \q No debiste burlarte de ellos el día en que estaban en angustia.

fr.L: Mais ne regarde pas le jour de ton frère, le jour de son malheur ; \q ne te réjouis pas au sujet des {{gender:enfants|fils}} de Juda le jour de leur ruine ; \q n’ouvre pas une grande bouche le jour de la détresse.
fr.B: Tu n’aurais pas dû te repaître du jour de ton frère, le jour de son malheur, \q ni te réjouir au sujet des gens de Juda le jour de leur ruine, \q ni te vanter si fort le jour de leur détresse.
fr.R: Tu n’aurais pas dû prendre plaisir à voir ton frère le jour où le malheur l’a frappé. \q Tu n’aurais pas dû te réjouir quand les gens de Juda ont été détruits. \q Tu n’aurais pas dû te vanter le jour où ils étaient dans la détresse.

sw.L: Lakini usitazame siku ya ndugu yako, siku ya balaa lake; \q usifurahie juu ya wana wa Yuda siku ya kuangamia kwao; \q usikuze kinywa chako siku ya taabu.
sw.B: Hukupaswa kufurahia kutazama siku ya ndugu yako, siku ya balaa lake, \q wala kuwafurahia watu wa Yuda siku ya kuangamia kwao, \q wala kujigamba sana siku ya taabu yao.
sw.R: Hukupaswa kufurahia kumwona ndugu yako siku ile balaa lilipompata. \q Hukupaswa kufurahi watu wa Yuda walipoangamizwa. \q Hukupaswa kujigamba siku ile walipokuwa katika taabu.

vi.L: Nhưng chớ nhìn ngày của anh em ngươi, ngày hoạn nạn của nó; \q chớ vui mừng về con cái Giu-đa trong ngày họ bị diệt vong; \q chớ há to miệng ngươi trong ngày khốn quẫn.
vi.B: Lẽ ra ngươi không được hả hê nhìn ngày của anh em ngươi, ngày hoạn nạn của nó, \q không được vui mừng về dân Giu-đa trong ngày họ bị diệt vong, \q không được khoác lác lớn tiếng trong ngày họ khốn quẫn.
vi.R: Lẽ ra ngươi không nên thích thú nhìn anh em mình trong ngày hoạn nạn đến với nó. \q Lẽ ra ngươi không nên vui mừng khi dân Giu-đa bị hủy diệt. \q Lẽ ra ngươi không nên khoe khoang trong ngày họ bị khốn quẫn.

ko.L: 그러나 너는 네 형제의 날, 그의 불행의 날을 구경하지 말아라. \q 유다 자손이 망하는 날에 그들을 두고 기뻐하지 말아라. \q 고난의 날에 네 입을 크게 벌리지 말아라.
ko.B: 너는 네 형제의 날, 그가 불행을 당한 날을 고소하다는 듯이 바라보지 말았어야 했다. \q 유다 백성이 망하던 날에 기뻐하지 말았어야 했고, \q 그들이 고난을 당하던 날에 그렇게 큰소리치지 말았어야 했다.
ko.R: 네 형제에게 불행이 닥친 날, 너는 그것을 보며 즐거워하지 말았어야 했다. \q 유다 백성이 멸망할 때 기뻐하지 말았어야 했다. \q 그들이 고난을 당하던 날에 뽐내지 말았어야 했다.

decisions.choice: do not look ... do not rejoice: commands spoken as if the day were still before Edom, condemning what it did
alternatives: warnings against doing these things in a disaster still to come
decisions.reason: Verses 12-14 are a series of eight commands, "do not ...". Verse 11 has already described the day as past, so the commands are taken as the prophet's vivid way of condemning what Edom did: he puts himself on that day and cries out against each act in turn. Some read them as warnings for the future. Either way, they set out what Edom is judged for.

decisions.choice: look on: gaze with pleasure; make your mouth big: boast, mock
decisions.reason: To "look on" someone's day of trouble is to watch it with satisfaction (Psalm 22:18; Micah 7:10). To "make the mouth big" is to speak proudly and mockingly (Ezekiel 35:13, again of Edom).

decisions.choice: the day: the day of disaster, named again and again
decisions.reason: The word "day" comes ten times in verses 11-14. The repetition fixes the reader on the one day of Judah's ruin, and leads to "the day of the LORD" in verse 15, when the day will turn on Edom.

decisions.choice: do not (L); You should not have (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the form of the commands. Balanced and Readable say what they mean here, a condemnation of past acts (m1), with "You should not have". Balanced says "gloated" and "boasted so loudly" for the idioms (m2); Readable says "enjoyed watching" and "bragged".

decisions.choice: "no mires ... no te alegres" (L); "No debiste ..." (B, R); "los hijos de Judá" (L) with no gender span
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the form of the commands; Balanced and Readable say what they mean here, a condemnation of past acts, as the English does. Spanish "hijos" already includes women, so it takes no gender span (terms note).

decisions.choice: "ne regarde pas ... ne te réjouis pas" (L); "Tu n’aurais pas dû ..." (B, R); "les {{gender:enfants|fils}} de Juda" (L)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the form of the commands; Balanced and Readable say what they mean here, a condemnation of past acts, as the English does. French has two real wordings for the sons of Judah, so Literal carries the gender setting, as the Pentateuch does.

decisions.choice: "usitazame ... usifurahie" (L); "Hukupaswa ..." (B, R); "wana wa Yuda" (L) with no gender span
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the form of the commands; Balanced and Readable say what they mean here, a condemnation of past acts, as the English does. "Wana" already covers both sexes, so Swahili writes no gender span.

decisions.choice: "chớ ..." (L); "Lẽ ra ngươi không được / không nên ..." (B, R); "con cái Giu-đa" (L) with no gender span
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the form of the commands; Balanced and Readable say what they mean here, a condemnation of past acts, as the English does. "Con cái" already covers both sexes. Judah, the wronged people, is "họ", as the oracles use it for Israel.

decisions.choice: "…하지 말아라" (L); "…하지 말았어야 했다" (B, R); "유다 자손" (L), "유다 백성" (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the form of the commands; Balanced and Readable say what they mean here, a condemnation of past acts, as the English does. "자손" and "백성" include women, so Korean needs no gender span.

source.text: אַל־תָּב֤וֹא בְשַֽׁעַר־עַמִּי֙ בְּי֣וֹם אֵידָ֔ם אַל־תֵּ֧רֶא גַם־אַתָּ֛ה בְּרָעָת֖וֹ בְּי֣וֹם אֵיד֑וֹ וְאַל־תִּשְׁלַ֥חְנָה בְחֵיל֖וֹ בְּי֥וֹם אֵידֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: Do not enter into [the] gate of my people on [the] day of their disaster; do not look, also you, on his calamity on [the] day of his disaster; and do not stretch out [a hand] on his wealth on [the] day of his disaster.

en.L: Do not enter the gate of my people on the day of their disaster; \q do not look, you too, on his calamity on the day of his disaster; \q and do not stretch out [your hand] against his wealth on the day of his disaster.
en.B: You should not have marched through the gate of my people on the day of their disaster, \q nor gloated, you of all people, over his calamity on the day of his disaster, \q nor seized his wealth on the day of his disaster.
en.R: You should not have marched through the gates of my people's city on the day disaster struck them. \q You, of all people, should not have enjoyed seeing them suffer on the day of their disaster. \q You should not have taken their wealth on the day of their disaster.

es.L: No entres por la puerta de {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} pueblo el día de su calamidad; \q no mires, tú también, su mal el día de su calamidad; \q y no extiendas [la mano] contra su riqueza el día de su calamidad.
es.B: No debiste entrar por la puerta de {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} pueblo el día de su calamidad, \q ni mirar con gozo, tú precisamente, su desgracia el día de su calamidad, \q ni apoderarte de su riqueza el día de su calamidad.
es.R: No debiste entrar por las puertas de la ciudad de {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} pueblo el día en que les llegó la calamidad. \q Tú, precisamente tú, no debiste disfrutar viéndolos sufrir el día de su calamidad. \q No debiste quitarles su riqueza el día de su calamidad.

fr.L: N’entre pas par la porte de {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} peuple le jour de son désastre ; \q ne regarde pas, toi aussi, son malheur le jour de son désastre ; \q et ne porte pas [la main] sur ses richesses le jour de son désastre.
fr.B: Tu n’aurais pas dû franchir la porte de {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} peuple le jour de son désastre, \q ni te repaître, toi entre tous, de son malheur le jour de son désastre, \q ni faire main basse sur ses richesses le jour de son désastre.
fr.R: Tu n’aurais pas dû entrer par les portes de la ville de {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} peuple le jour où le désastre l’a frappé. \q Toi entre tous, tu n’aurais pas dû prendre plaisir à les voir souffrir le jour de leur désastre. \q Tu n’aurais pas dû prendre leurs richesses le jour de leur désastre.

sw.L: Usiingie katika lango la watu {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}} siku ya msiba wao; \q usitazame, wewe pia, mabaya yake siku ya msiba wake; \q wala usinyooshe [mkono] juu ya mali yake siku ya msiba wake.
sw.B: Hukupaswa kuingia katika lango la watu {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}} siku ya msiba wao, \q wala wewe, kati ya wote, kufurahia kutazama mabaya yake siku ya msiba wake, \q wala kunyakua mali yake siku ya msiba wake.
sw.R: Hukupaswa kuingia kupitia malango ya mji wa watu {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}} siku ile msiba ulipowapata. \q Wewe, kati ya wote, hukupaswa kufurahia kuwaona wakiteseka siku ya msiba wao. \q Hukupaswa kuchukua mali zao siku ya msiba wao.

vi.L: Chớ vào cổng của dân {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} trong ngày tai họa của họ; \q chớ nhìn, cả ngươi nữa, sự khốn khổ của nó trong ngày tai họa của nó; \q và chớ đưa [tay] lấy của cải nó trong ngày tai họa của nó.
vi.B: Lẽ ra ngươi không được kéo vào cổng của dân {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} trong ngày tai họa của họ, \q không được hả hê, chính ngươi, nhìn sự khốn khổ của nó trong ngày tai họa của nó, \q không được chiếm đoạt của cải nó trong ngày tai họa của nó.
vi.R: Lẽ ra ngươi không nên vào qua các cổng thành của dân {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} trong ngày tai họa đến với họ. \q Chính ngươi lại càng không nên thích thú nhìn họ đau khổ trong ngày tai họa của họ. \q Lẽ ra ngươi không nên lấy của cải họ trong ngày tai họa của họ.

ko.L: 내 백성이 재앙을 당하는 날에 그들의 성문으로 들어가지 말아라. \q 너마저 그가 재앙을 당하는 날에 그의 환난을 구경하지 말아라. \q 그가 재앙을 당하는 날에 그의 재물에 [손을] 대지 말아라.
ko.B: 너는 내 백성이 재앙을 당하던 날에 그들의 성문으로 쳐들어가지 말았어야 했다. \q 너만은 그가 재앙을 당하던 날에 그의 환난을 고소하게 바라보지 말았어야 했고, \q 그가 재앙을 당하던 날에 그의 재물을 빼앗지 말았어야 했다.
ko.R: 내 백성에게 재앙이 닥친 날, 너는 그들의 성문으로 들어가지 말았어야 했다. \q 다른 누구도 아닌 네가, 재앙의 날에 그들이 고통당하는 것을 보며 즐거워하지 말았어야 했다. \q 재앙의 날에 그들의 재물을 빼앗지 말았어야 했다.

decisions.choice: the day of his disaster, three times: a play on the name Edom
decisions.reason: The word for disaster in these lines sounds like the name Edom, and it comes three times, at the end of each line. The sound ties Edom's name to Judah's ruin, and the reader is left to hear that Edom's own disaster is coming (verse 15).

decisions.choice: my people: the LORD speaks
decisions.reason: The oracle began "Thus says the Lord GOD" (verse 1), and here the speaker calls Judah "my people". Edom's wrong was done to the LORD's own people.

decisions.choice: stretch out: stretch out the hand to seize
decisions.reason: The verb is used without its object, "hand", as it sometimes is (2 Samuel 6:6). Its form is unusual, and some read it as a slip for the usual form "you"; the sense is the same: Edom took part in the looting. "You too" in the second line means "you, of all people", the brother.

decisions.choice: do not (L); You should not have (B, R); disaster (all levels)
decisions.reason: As in verse 12, Balanced and Readable state the commands as condemnation. Every level keeps "disaster" at the end of each line, so the repetition can be heard (m1). Readable says "my people's city" for "the gate of my people", and "them" for "his", since Judah is meant.

decisions.choice: "calamidad" at the end of each line, at every level
decisions.reason: The Hebrew repeats the same word, which sounds like the name Edom, at the end of each line (meaning decision), so Spanish keeps one word three times; "calamidad" is the word Spanish Jeremiah 49:8 uses for Esau's own disaster. God's "mi pueblo" takes a deity_pronoun span, as everywhere in the Spanish prophets.

decisions.choice: "désastre" at the end of each line, at every level
decisions.reason: The Hebrew repeats one word, which sounds like the name Edom, at the end of each line (meaning decision), so French keeps one word three times; "désastre" is the word of the French Jeremiah 49:8 for Esau's own disaster. God's "mon peuple" takes a deity_pronoun span, as French does for every first-person possessive of God.

decisions.choice: "msiba" at the end of each line, at every level
decisions.reason: The Hebrew repeats one word, which sounds like the name Edom, at the end of each line (meaning decision), so Swahili keeps one word three times; "msiba" is the word of the Swahili Jeremiah 49:8 for Esau's own disaster. The deity_pronoun span stands on the free possessive "wangu".

decisions.choice: "tai họa" at the end of each line, at every level
decisions.reason: The Hebrew repeats one word, which sounds like the name Edom, at the end of each line (meaning decision), so the Vietnamese keeps one word three times; "tai họa" is the word of the Vietnamese Jeremiah 49:8 for Esau's own disaster.

decisions.choice: "재앙" in each line, at every level
decisions.reason: The Hebrew repeats one word, which sounds like the name Edom, at the end of each line (meaning decision); Korean, which puts the verb last, cannot end each line with it but keeps the one word three times. "재앙" is the word of the Korean Jeremiah 49:8 for Esau's own disaster.

source.text: וְאַֽל־תַּעֲמֹד֙ עַל־הַפֶּ֔רֶק לְהַכְרִ֖ית אֶת־פְּלִיטָ֑יו וְאַל־תַּסְגֵּ֥ר שְׂרִידָ֖יו בְּי֥וֹם צָרָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And do not stand at the crossing to cut off his fugitives; and do not hand over his survivors on [the] day of distress.

en.L: And do not stand at the crossroads \q to cut off his fugitives; \q and do not hand over his survivors on the day of distress.
en.B: You should not have stood at the crossroads \q to cut down those who escaped, \q nor handed over his survivors on the day of distress.
en.R: You should not have waited where the roads meet to kill those who were running away. \q You should not have handed over the survivors to their enemies on that day of distress.

es.L: Y no te pares en la encrucijada \q para exterminar a sus fugitivos; \q y no entregues a sus sobrevivientes el día de la angustia.
es.B: No debiste apostarte en la encrucijada \q para matar a los que escapaban, \q ni entregar a sus sobrevivientes el día de la angustia.
es.R: No debiste esperar donde se cruzan los caminos para matar a los que huían. \q No debiste entregar a los sobrevivientes a sus enemigos en aquel día de angustia.

fr.L: Et ne te tiens pas au carrefour \q pour retrancher ses fuyards ; \q et ne livre pas ses survivants le jour de la détresse.
fr.B: Tu n’aurais pas dû te poster au carrefour \q pour abattre ceux qui s’échappaient, \q ni livrer ses survivants le jour de la détresse.
fr.R: Tu n’aurais pas dû attendre là où les routes se croisent pour tuer ceux qui s’enfuyaient. \q Tu n’aurais pas dû livrer les survivants à leurs ennemis en ce jour de détresse.

sw.L: Wala usisimame njia panda \q ili kuwakatilia mbali wakimbizi wake; \q wala usiwatoe waliosalia wake siku ya taabu.
sw.B: Hukupaswa kusimama njia panda \q ili kuwaua wale waliokuwa wakikimbia, \q wala kuwatoa waliosalia wake siku ya taabu.
sw.R: Hukupaswa kungoja mahali njia zinapokutana ili kuwaua wale waliokuwa wakikimbia. \q Hukupaswa kuwakabidhi kwa adui zao wale walionusurika siku ile ya taabu.

vi.L: Và chớ đứng nơi ngã ba đường \q để diệt những kẻ chạy trốn của nó; \q và chớ nộp những kẻ sống sót của nó trong ngày khốn quẫn.
vi.B: Lẽ ra ngươi không được đứng chặn nơi ngã ba đường \q để giết những người trốn thoát, \q không được nộp những người sống sót của nó trong ngày khốn quẫn.
vi.R: Lẽ ra ngươi không nên chờ ở chỗ các con đường gặp nhau để giết những người đang chạy trốn. \q Lẽ ra ngươi không nên nộp những người sống sót cho kẻ thù của họ trong ngày khốn quẫn ấy.

ko.L: 갈림길에 서서 \q 그의 도망치는 자들을 끊어 버리지 말아라. \q 고난의 날에 그의 살아남은 자들을 넘겨주지 말아라.
ko.B: 너는 갈림길에 서서 \q 도망치는 사람들을 죽이지 말았어야 했고, \q 고난의 날에 그의 살아남은 사람들을 넘겨주지 말았어야 했다.
ko.R: 너는 길이 만나는 곳에서 기다리다가 도망치는 사람들을 죽이지 말았어야 했다. \q 그 고난의 날에 살아남은 사람들을 원수들에게 넘겨주지 말았어야 했다.

decisions.choice: the crossroads: a place where the road divides, where fugitives could be stopped
decisions.reason: The word is rare. It seems to mean a fork or a parting of the ways, where those fleeing Jerusalem would have to pass. Some take it as a narrow pass. Edom waited where the escaping people would come.

decisions.choice: hand over his survivors: deliver them to the enemy
decisions.reason: The verb means to shut up, and so to hand someone over into another's power (Amos 1:6, 9, where Philistia and Tyre hand over whole communities to Edom). Edom caught the survivors and gave them up to the conquerors.

decisions.choice: You should not have (B, R); to their enemies (R)
decisions.reason: As in verses 12-13, Balanced and Readable state the commands as condemnation. Readable says to whom the survivors were handed over (m2), and "where the roads meet" for the crossroads.

source.text: כִּֽי־קָר֥וֹב יוֹם־יְהוָ֖ה עַל־כָּל־הַגּוֹיִ֑ם כַּאֲשֶׁ֤ר עָשִׂ֨יתָ֙ יֵעָ֣שֶׂה לָּ֔ךְ גְּמֻלְךָ֖ יָשׁ֥וּב בְּרֹאשֶֽׁךָ׃

records.literal_gloss: For near [is the] day of Yahweh on all the nations; as you have done, it will be done to you; your dealing will return on your head.

en.L: For near [is] the day of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} upon all the nations; \q just as you have done, it will be done to you; \q your dealing will return on your own head.
en.B: For the day of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} is close at hand for all the nations. \q As you have done, so it will be done to you; \q what you have dealt out will come back on your own head.
en.R: The day of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} is near for all the nations. \q What you did to others will be done to you. \q The harm you did will come back on you.

es.L: Porque cerca [está] el día {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} sobre todas las naciones; \q como tú hiciste, se te hará; \q tu obra volverá sobre tu cabeza.
es.B: Porque el día {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} está cerca para todas las naciones. \q Como tú hiciste, así se te hará; \q lo que hiciste caerá sobre tu propia cabeza.
es.R: El día {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} está cerca para todas las naciones. \q Lo que hiciste a otros se te hará a ti. \q El mal que hiciste caerá sobre ti.

fr.L: Car il est proche, le jour {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}, sur toutes les nations ; \q comme tu as fait, il te sera fait ; \q ce que tu as fait retombera sur ta tête.
fr.B: Car le jour {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} est tout proche pour toutes les nations. \q Comme tu as fait, ainsi il te sera fait ; \q ce que tu as infligé retombera sur ta propre tête.
fr.R: Le jour {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} est proche pour toutes les nations. \q Ce que tu as fait aux autres, on te le fera. \q Le mal que tu as fait retombera sur toi.

sw.L: Kwa maana siku ya {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} [i] karibu juu ya mataifa yote; \q kama ulivyotenda, ndivyo utakavyotendewa; \q matendo yako yatakurudia juu ya kichwa chako.
sw.B: Kwa maana siku ya {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} imekaribia kwa mataifa yote. \q Kama ulivyotenda, ndivyo utakavyotendewa; \q ulichowatendea wengine kitarudi juu ya kichwa chako mwenyewe.
sw.R: Siku ya {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} iko karibu kwa mataifa yote. \q Ulichowatendea wengine, utatendewa wewe. \q Mabaya uliyotenda yatakurudia wewe mwenyewe.

vi.L: Vì ngày của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đã gần trên mọi dân tộc; \q ngươi đã làm thế nào, người ta sẽ làm cho ngươi thế ấy; \q việc ngươi làm sẽ đổ lại trên đầu ngươi.
vi.B: Vì ngày của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đã gần kề cho mọi dân tộc. \q Ngươi đã làm thế nào, ngươi sẽ bị làm lại thế ấy; \q những gì ngươi gây ra sẽ đổ lại trên chính đầu ngươi.
vi.R: Ngày của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đã gần cho mọi dân tộc. \q Ngươi đã làm gì cho người khác, ngươi cũng sẽ bị làm như vậy. \q Điều ác ngươi đã làm sẽ quay lại trên ngươi.

ko.L: {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 날이 모든 민족 위에 가깝기 때문이다. \q 네가 행한 대로 너에게도 행해질 것이다. \q 네 행위가 네 머리 위로 돌아갈 것이다.
ko.B: {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 날이 모든 민족에게 가까이 왔다. \q 네가 한 그대로 너도 당할 것이다. \q 네가 남에게 한 일이 네 머리 위로 되돌아갈 것이다.
ko.R: {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 날이 모든 민족에게 가까이 왔다. \q 네가 남에게 한 대로 너도 당할 것이다. \q 네가 저지른 악이 너에게 되돌아올 것이다.

decisions.choice: the day of the LORD: the day when the LORD comes to judge
decisions.reason: The prophets speak of "the day of the LORD" as the time when God acts in judgment, against the nations and against his own people when they sin (Isaiah 13:6; Joel 1:15; Amos 5:18). Here Edom's day of judgment, "that day" of verse 8, becomes part of the LORD's day on all nations. The day Edom watched in verses 11-14 was Judah's; now the day is the LORD's.

decisions.choice: as you have done, it will be done to you: Edom will be repaid in kind
decisions.reason: The punishment matches the crime (compare Jeremiah 50:15, 29; Ezekiel 35:15). "Your dealing" is what Edom did to others, which will come back "on your own head", that is, on Edom itself (Joel 4:4, 7).

decisions.choice: the day of the LORD, at every level
decisions.reason: As set for the prophets, "the day of the LORD" is kept word for word at every level (Isaiah 13:6), so that the reader can follow the phrase through the books. Readable says "on you" for "on your own head".

decisions.choice: "el día del SEÑOR" at every level; "cerca [está]" (L), "está cerca" (B, R)
decisions.reason: The day of the LORD keeps one wording at every level, as Isaiah 13:6 and Joel 1:15 in Spanish, so the reader can follow the phrase through the prophets.

decisions.choice: "il est proche, le jour du SEIGNEUR" (L); "le jour du SEIGNEUR est tout proche" (B); "est proche" (R)
decisions.reason: The day of the LORD keeps one wording at every level, and the line follows the French of Isaiah 13:6 and Joel 1:15, so the reader can follow the phrase through the prophets.

decisions.choice: "siku ya BWANA [i] karibu" (L); "imekaribia" (B); "iko karibu" (R)
decisions.reason: The day of the LORD keeps one wording at every level, and the line follows the Swahili of Isaiah 13:6 and Joel 1:15, so the reader can follow the phrase through the prophets.

decisions.choice: "ngày của CHÚA đã gần" (L, R), "đã gần kề" (B)
decisions.reason: The day of the LORD keeps one wording at every level, as the published Isaiah 13:6 and Joel 1:15, so the reader can follow the phrase through the prophets.

decisions.choice: "{{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 날이 … 가깝다 / 가까이 왔다"
decisions.reason: The day of the LORD keeps one wording at every level, as the published Isaiah 13:6 and Joel 1:15, so the reader can follow the phrase through the prophets.

source.text: כִּ֗י כַּֽאֲשֶׁ֤ר שְׁתִיתֶם֙ עַל־הַ֣ר קָדְשִׁ֔י יִשְׁתּ֥וּ כָֽל־הַגּוֹיִ֖ם תָּמִ֑יד וְשָׁת֣וּ וְלָע֔וּ וְהָי֖וּ כְּל֥וֹא הָיֽוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: For just as you have drunk on my holy mountain, all the nations will drink continually; and they will drink and swallow, and they will be as [if] they had not been.

en.L: For just as you have drunk on my holy mountain, \q all the nations will drink continually; \q they will drink and gulp down, \q and they will be as though they had never been.
en.B: Just as you drank on my holy mountain, \q all the nations will keep on drinking; \q they will drink and gulp it down, \q and be as if they had never existed.
en.R: Just as you drank on my holy mountain, \q all the nations will keep drinking the cup of my anger. \q They will drink it all down, \q and they will disappear as if they had never lived.

es.L: Porque así como {{plural_you:ustedes han bebido|vosotros habéis bebido}} en {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} monte santo, \q beberán todas las naciones continuamente; \q beberán y tragarán, \q y serán como si no hubieran sido.
es.B: Así como {{plural_you:ustedes bebieron|vosotros bebisteis}} en {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} monte santo, \q todas las naciones beberán sin cesar; \q beberán y tragarán, \q y serán como si nunca hubieran existido.
es.R: Así como {{plural_you:ustedes bebieron|vosotros bebisteis}} en {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} monte santo, \q todas las naciones seguirán bebiendo la copa de {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} ira. \q La beberán hasta el fondo, \q y desaparecerán como si nunca hubieran vivido.

fr.L: Car, comme vous avez bu sur {{deity_pronoun:ma|Ma}} montagne sainte, \q toutes les nations boiront continuellement ; \q elles boiront et avaleront, \q et elles seront comme si elles n’avaient pas été.
fr.B: Comme vous avez bu sur {{deity_pronoun:ma|Ma}} montagne sainte, \q toutes les nations boiront sans cesse ; \q elles boiront à longs traits, \q et seront comme si elles n’avaient jamais existé.
fr.R: Comme vous avez bu sur {{deity_pronoun:ma|Ma}} montagne sainte, \q toutes les nations boiront sans arrêt la coupe de {{deity_pronoun:ma|Ma}} colère. \q Elles la boiront jusqu’au fond, \q et elles disparaîtront comme si elles n’avaient jamais vécu.

sw.L: Kwa maana kama mlivyokunywa juu ya mlima {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}} mtakatifu, \q mataifa yote yatakunywa daima; \q yatakunywa na kugugumia, \q nayo yatakuwa kana kwamba hayakuwahi kuwako.
sw.B: Kama mlivyokunywa juu ya mlima {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}} mtakatifu, \q mataifa yote yataendelea kunywa; \q yatakunywa na kugugumia, \q na kuwa kana kwamba hayakuwahi kuwako.
sw.R: Kama mlivyokunywa juu ya mlima {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}} mtakatifu, \q mataifa yote yataendelea kunywa kikombe cha hasira {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}}. \q Yatakinywa chote, \q nayo yatatoweka kana kwamba hayakuwahi kuishi.

vi.L: Vì như các ngươi đã uống trên núi thánh của {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, \q mọi dân tộc sẽ uống mãi; \q chúng sẽ uống và nuốt, \q và chúng sẽ như chưa hề có.
vi.B: Như các ngươi đã uống trên núi thánh của {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, \q mọi dân tộc sẽ cứ uống mãi; \q chúng sẽ uống và nốc cạn, \q và sẽ như chưa từng có.
vi.R: Như các ngươi đã uống trên núi thánh của {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, \q mọi dân tộc sẽ cứ phải uống chén thịnh nộ của {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}. \q Chúng sẽ uống cạn chén ấy, \q và sẽ biến mất như chưa hề sống.

ko.L: 너희가 내 거룩한 산에서 마신 것처럼, \q 모든 민족이 끊임없이 마실 것이다. \q 그들이 마시고 삼켜서, \q 본래 없었던 것처럼 될 것이다.
ko.B: 너희가 내 거룩한 산에서 마셨듯이, \q 모든 민족이 계속 마실 것이다. \q 그들이 마시고 들이켜서, \q 처음부터 없었던 것처럼 될 것이다.
ko.R: 너희가 내 거룩한 산에서 마셨듯이, \q 모든 민족이 내 분노의 잔을 계속 마실 것이다. \q 그들은 그 잔을 다 들이켜고, \q 처음부터 없었던 것처럼 사라질 것이다.

decisions.choice: you have drunk: "you" is now plural, and who is meant is not said
alternatives: the people of Judah, who drank the cup of judgment when Jerusalem fell
the Edomites, who drank in celebration on the captured mountain
decisions.reason: Until now Edom has been "you" in the singular; here the verb is plural. Read as Judah, the verse says that as God's own people drank the cup of his anger on Mount Zion, so all the nations will drink it now (Jeremiah 25:28-29; 49:12). Read as Edom, it says that as they caroused on God's mountain after its fall, so the nations will drink the cup of judgment. The Hebrew allows both, and the drinking of the nations is judgment either way.

decisions.choice: the nations will drink: the cup of God's wrath
decisions.reason: The prophets picture judgment as a cup of wine that God makes the nations drink until they stagger and fall (Isaiah 51:17-23; Jeremiah 25:15-29; 49:12, where Edom must drink it; Lamentations 4:21).

decisions.choice: swallow: gulp down
decisions.reason: The verb is rare. It seems to mean gulping down, drinking the cup to the last drop. Some take it as reeling or talking wildly, as drunkards do. In both readings the drinking ends in the nations' disappearance.

decisions.choice: the cup of my anger (R)
decisions.reason: Readable names the cup, which the verse implies (m2), so the reader can see that the drinking is judgment. It keeps "you drank" without saying who "you" are (m1).

decisions.choice: plural_you on "ustedes bebieron" / "vosotros bebisteis"
decisions.reason: The Hebrew "you" turns plural here, without saying who is meant (meaning decision), so Spanish leaves the subject open and marks only the number, with a plural_you span. "La copa" at Readable is the word of Spanish Jeremiah 49:12.

decisions.choice: "vous" for the plural "you have drunk"
decisions.reason: The Hebrew turns from the singular to the plural here without saying who is meant (meaning decision); French follows the number with "vous" and leaves the reference open. "La coupe" at Readable is the word of the French Jeremiah 49:12.

decisions.choice: plural "mlivyokunywa"
decisions.reason: The Hebrew turns from the singular to the plural here without saying who is meant (meaning decision); Swahili marks the plural in the verb and leaves the reference open. "Kikombe" at Readable is the word of the Swahili Jeremiah 49:12.

decisions.choice: plural "các ngươi"
decisions.reason: The Hebrew turns from the singular to the plural here without saying who is meant (meaning decision); Vietnamese follows the number with "các ngươi" and leaves the reference open. "Chén" at Readable is the word of the Vietnamese Jeremiah 49:12.

decisions.choice: plural "너희"
decisions.reason: The Hebrew turns from the singular to the plural here without saying who is meant (meaning decision); Korean follows the number with "너희" and leaves the reference open. "잔" at Readable is the word of the Korean Jeremiah 49:12.

source.text: וּבְהַ֥ר צִיּ֛וֹן תִּהְיֶ֥ה פְלֵיטָ֖ה וְהָ֣יָה קֹ֑דֶשׁ וְיָֽרְשׁוּ֙ בֵּ֣ית יַֽעֲקֹ֔ב אֵ֖ת מוֹרָֽשֵׁיהֶם׃

records.literal_gloss: And on Mount Zion will be escape, and it will be holy; and will possess [the] house of Jacob their possessions.

en.L: But on Mount Zion there will be escape, and it will be holy; \q and the house of Jacob will possess their possessions.
en.B: But on Mount Zion there will be survivors, and it will be holy; \q and the house of Jacob will take possession of what belongs to them.
en.R: But on Mount Zion some people will escape, and it will be a holy place. \q The people of Jacob will take back the land that belongs to them.

es.L: Pero en el monte Sion habrá quienes escapen, y será santo; \q y la casa de Jacob poseerá sus posesiones.
es.B: Pero en el monte Sion habrá sobrevivientes, y será santo; \q y la casa de Jacob tomará posesión de lo que le pertenece.
es.R: Pero en el monte Sion algunos escaparán, y será un lugar santo. \q El pueblo de Jacob recuperará la tierra que le pertenece.

fr.L: Mais sur le mont Sion il y aura des rescapés, et il sera saint ; \q et la maison de Jacob possédera ses possessions.
fr.B: Mais sur le mont Sion il y aura des survivants, et ce sera un lieu saint ; \q et la maison de Jacob prendra possession de ce qui lui appartient.
fr.R: Mais sur le mont Sion, des gens échapperont, et ce sera un lieu saint. \q Le peuple de Jacob reprendra le pays qui lui appartient.

sw.L: Lakini katika mlima Sayuni kutakuwa na watakaookoka, nao utakuwa mtakatifu; \q na nyumba ya Yakobo itamiliki milki zao.
sw.B: Lakini katika mlima Sayuni kutakuwa na watakaonusurika, nao utakuwa mtakatifu; \q na nyumba ya Yakobo itamiliki kile kilicho chao.
sw.R: Lakini katika mlima Sayuni baadhi ya watu wataokoka, nao utakuwa mahali patakatifu. \q Watu wa Yakobo wataichukua tena nchi iliyo yao.

vi.L: Nhưng trên núi Si-ôn sẽ có [những người] thoát nạn, và núi ấy sẽ là thánh; \q và nhà Gia-cốp sẽ chiếm hữu sản nghiệp của mình.
vi.B: Nhưng trên núi Si-ôn sẽ có những người sống sót, và núi ấy sẽ là thánh; \q và nhà Gia-cốp sẽ chiếm lại những gì thuộc về mình.
vi.R: Nhưng trên núi Si-ôn một số người sẽ thoát nạn, và núi ấy sẽ là nơi thánh. \q Dân Gia-cốp sẽ lấy lại đất đai thuộc về mình.

ko.L: 그러나 시온산에는 피하는 [사람들이] 있을 것이고, 그곳은 거룩할 것이다. \q 야곱 집이 자기들의 소유를 차지할 것이다.
ko.B: 그러나 시온산에는 살아남은 사람들이 있을 것이고, 그곳은 거룩한 곳이 될 것이다. \q 야곱 집이 자기들에게 속한 것을 차지할 것이다.
ko.R: 그러나 시온산에서는 몇몇 사람이 피할 것이고, 그곳은 거룩한 곳이 될 것이다. \q 야곱의 자손이 자기들의 땅을 되찾을 것이다.

decisions.choice: escape: a place of escape, and those who escape
decisions.reason: The word means escape and also the people who escape, the survivors. Edom cut off Judah's fugitives (verse 14); now Mount Zion will hold survivors. Joel 3:5 takes up the same words: "on Mount Zion and in Jerusalem there will be those who escape, as the LORD has said".

decisions.choice: it will be holy: Zion will again be the LORD's holy place
decisions.reason: The nations defiled God's holy mountain (verse 16); now it will be holy again, set apart for the LORD, and foreigners will no longer pass through it (Joel 4:17).

decisions.choice: their possessions: the house of Jacob will take back its own land
decisions.reason: With different vowels the same letters can be read "those who dispossessed them", so that Jacob takes possession of the peoples who had taken its land. The Greek translation reads it that way. The Hebrew text as written is followed; verses 19-20 describe Israel taking back its own land and more. This description of the Greek is written from general knowledge.

decisions.choice: the land that belongs to them (R)
decisions.reason: The word for possessions is used of an inheritance, especially of land (Deuteronomy 2:5, where the same root describes Esau's own land). Readable says "land" because verses 19-20 show that land is meant, and "take back" because it was theirs.

decisions.choice: "habrá quienes escapen" (L); "algunos escaparán" (R)
decisions.reason: Joel 3:5 takes up these words, and its Spanish says "habrá [quienes] escapen" and "algunos escaparán"; Obadiah uses the same wording so that the link can be seen.

decisions.choice: "il y aura des rescapés" (L); "des gens échapperont" (R)
decisions.reason: Joel 3:5 takes up these words, and its French says "sur le mont Sion ... il y aura des rescapés" and "des gens échapperont"; Obadiah uses the same wording so the link can be seen.

decisions.choice: "kutakuwa na watakaookoka" (L); "baadhi ya watu wataokoka" (R)
decisions.reason: Joel 3:5 takes up these words, and its Swahili says "katika mlima Sayuni ... kutakuwa na [watakaookoka]" and "baadhi ya watu ... wataokoka"; Obadiah uses the same wording so the link can be seen.

decisions.choice: "sẽ có [những người] thoát nạn" (L); "một số người sẽ thoát nạn" (R)
decisions.reason: Joel 3:5 takes up these words, and its Vietnamese says "trên núi Si-ôn ... sẽ có [những người] thoát nạn" and "Một số người ... sẽ thoát nạn"; Obadiah uses the same wording so the link can be seen.

decisions.choice: "피하는 [사람들이] 있을 것이고" (L); "몇몇 사람이 피할 것이고" (R)
decisions.reason: Joel 3:5 takes up these words, and its Korean says "시온산과 예루살렘에 피하는 [사람들이] 있을 것" and "몇몇 사람이 피할 것이다"; Obadiah uses the same wording so the link can be seen.

source.text: וְהָיָה֩ בֵית־יַעֲקֹ֨ב אֵ֜שׁ וּבֵ֧ית יוֹסֵ֣ף לֶהָבָ֗ה וּבֵ֤ית עֵשָׂו֙ לְקַ֔שׁ וְדָלְק֥וּ בָהֶ֖ם וַאֲכָל֑וּם וְלֹֽא־יִֽהְיֶ֤השָׂרִיד֙ לְבֵ֣ית עֵשָׂ֔ו כִּ֥י יְהוָ֖ה דִּבֵּֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: And will be [the] house of Jacob a fire, and [the] house of Joseph a flame, and [the] house of Esau stubble; and they will burn among them and consume them, and there will not be a survivor to [the] house of Esau, for Yahweh has spoken.

en.L: And the house of Jacob will be fire, and the house of Joseph flame, and the house of Esau [will be] stubble; \q they will set them ablaze and consume them, \q and there will be no survivor for the house of Esau, \q for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has spoken.
en.B: The house of Jacob will become a fire, and the house of Joseph will be a flame, and the house of Esau will be stubble; \q they will set them ablaze and burn them up. \q No survivor will be left to the house of Esau, \q for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has spoken.
en.R: Jacob's people will be a fire and Joseph's people a flame, and the house of Esau will be like dry straw. \q Jacob's people will set them on fire and burn them up. \q No one from the house of Esau will survive. \q {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} has said this!

es.L: Y la casa de Jacob será fuego, y la casa de José llama, y la casa de Esaú [será] rastrojo; \q los encenderán y los consumirán, \q y no quedará sobreviviente de la casa de Esaú, \q porque {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} ha hablado.
es.B: La casa de Jacob se convertirá en fuego, y la casa de José en llama, y la casa de Esaú será rastrojo; \q le prenderán fuego y la consumirán. \q No le quedará sobreviviente a la casa de Esaú, \q porque {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} ha hablado.
es.R: El pueblo de Jacob será un fuego y el pueblo de José una llama, y la casa de Esaú será como paja seca. \q El pueblo de Jacob le prenderá fuego y la quemará por completo. \q Nadie de la casa de Esaú sobrevivirá. \q ¡{{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} lo ha dicho!

fr.L: Et la maison de Jacob sera un feu, et la maison de Joseph une flamme, et la maison d’Ésaü [sera] du chaume ; \q ils l’embraseront et la consumeront, \q et il n’y aura pas de survivant pour la maison d’Ésaü, \q car {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} a parlé.
fr.B: La maison de Jacob deviendra un feu, la maison de Joseph une flamme, et la maison d’Ésaü du chaume ; \q ils l’embraseront et la dévoreront. \q Il ne restera pas de survivant à la maison d’Ésaü, \q car {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} a parlé.
fr.R: Le peuple de Jacob sera un feu et le peuple de Joseph une flamme, et la maison d’Ésaü sera comme de la paille sèche. \q Le peuple de Jacob y mettra le feu et la brûlera entièrement. \q Personne de la maison d’Ésaü ne survivra. \q C’est {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} qui l’a dit !

sw.L: Na nyumba ya Yakobo itakuwa moto, na nyumba ya Yusufu mwali wa moto, na nyumba ya Esau [itakuwa] mabua; \q wataiwasha na kuiteketeza, \q wala hapatakuwa na aliyesalia wa nyumba ya Esau, \q kwa maana {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} amesema.
sw.B: Nyumba ya Yakobo itakuwa moto, na nyumba ya Yusufu itakuwa mwali wa moto, na nyumba ya Esau itakuwa mabua; \q wataiwasha moto na kuiteketeza. \q Hakuna atakayesalia wa nyumba ya Esau, \q kwa maana {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} amesema.
sw.R: Watu wa Yakobo watakuwa moto na watu wa Yusufu mwali wa moto, na nyumba ya Esau itakuwa kama nyasi kavu. \q Watu wa Yakobo wataiwasha moto na kuiteketeza kabisa. \q Hakuna mtu wa nyumba ya Esau atakayenusurika. \q {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} amesema hivyo!

vi.L: Và nhà Gia-cốp sẽ là lửa, nhà Giô-sép là ngọn lửa, và nhà Ê-sau [sẽ là] rơm rạ; \q họ sẽ đốt cháy và thiêu nuốt nó, \q và nhà Ê-sau sẽ không còn ai sống sót, \q vì {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đã phán.
vi.B: Nhà Gia-cốp sẽ thành lửa, nhà Giô-sép thành ngọn lửa, còn nhà Ê-sau sẽ là rơm rạ; \q họ sẽ châm lửa đốt và thiêu rụi nó. \q Nhà Ê-sau sẽ không còn ai sống sót, \q vì {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đã phán.
vi.R: Dân Gia-cốp sẽ là lửa và dân Giô-sép là ngọn lửa, còn nhà Ê-sau sẽ như rơm khô. \q Dân Gia-cốp sẽ đốt nó cháy rụi. \q Không ai trong nhà Ê-sau sẽ sống sót. \q {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đã phán vậy!

ko.L: 야곱 집은 불이 되고, 요셉 집은 불꽃이 되며, 에서 집은 지푸라기가 [될 것이다]. \q 그들이 그것을 불사르고 삼킬 것이니, \q 에서 집에는 살아남는 자가 없을 것이다. \q {{divine_name:주|야훼}}가 말하였기 때문이다.
ko.B: 야곱 집은 불이 되고, 요셉 집은 불꽃이 되며, 에서 집은 지푸라기가 될 것이다. \q 그들이 에서 집을 불살라 태워 버릴 것이다. \q 에서 집에는 살아남는 사람이 하나도 없을 것이다. \q 나 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}가 말했다.
ko.R: 야곱의 자손은 불이 되고 요셉의 자손은 불꽃이 될 것이다. 에서 집은 마른 지푸라기 같을 것이다. \q 야곱의 자손이 에서 집에 불을 놓아 다 태워 버릴 것이다. \q 에서 집에서는 아무도 살아남지 못할 것이다. \q 나 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}가 말했다!

decisions.choice: the house of Jacob and the house of Joseph: the whole people of Israel, south and north
decisions.reason: Joseph, the father of Ephraim and Manasseh, stands for the northern tribes (Amos 5:6; Ezekiel 37:16-19). With the house of Jacob beside it, the verse pictures the whole people reunited and acting together against Esau.

decisions.choice: fire, flame and stubble: a picture of swift, complete destruction
decisions.reason: Stubble, the dry stalks left after the harvest, burns at once (Exodus 15:7; Isaiah 5:24; Malachi 3:19). The brother who stood by while Jacob burned is now himself the fuel.

decisions.choice: for the LORD has spoken: the closing seal on the oracle
decisions.reason: The phrase marks a word as certain, because it is the LORD's (Isaiah 1:20; Joel 4:8). "No survivor" answers verse 14, where Edom handed over Judah's survivors.

decisions.choice: stubble (L, B); dry straw (R); survivor
decisions.reason: Readable says "dry straw" for stubble, which may be an unfamiliar word, and makes "they" plain as Jacob's people. Every level keeps "the house of Esau".

decisions.choice: "{{divine_name:주|야훼}}가 말하였기 때문이다" (L); "나 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}가 말했다" (B, R), without -시-
decisions.reason: The closing seal belongs to God's own oracle, so his name takes no -시-, as in Joel 4:8; Balanced and Readable make the speaker plain with "나".

source.text: וְיָרְשׁ֨וּ הַנֶּ֜גֶב אֶת־הַ֣ר עֵשָׂ֗ו וְהַשְּׁפֵלָה֙ אֶת־פְּלִשְׁתִּ֔ים וְיָרְשׁוּ֙ אֶת־שְׂדֵ֣ה אֶפְרַ֔יִם וְאֵ֖ת שְׂדֵ֣ה שֹׁמְר֑וֹן וּבִנְיָמִ֖ן אֶת־הַגִּלְעָֽד׃

records.literal_gloss: And they will possess the Negev, [the] mountain of Esau, and the Shephelah, [the] Philistines; and they will possess [the] field of Ephraim and [the] field of Samaria, and Benjamin, the Gilead.

en.L: And [those of] the Negev will possess Mount Esau, and [those of] the Shephelah the Philistines; \q and they will possess the territory of Ephraim \q and the territory of Samaria, \q and Benjamin [will possess] Gilead.
en.B: The people of the Negev will take possession of Mount Esau, and the people of the Shephelah the land of the Philistines; \q they will take possession of the territory of Ephraim \q and the territory of Samaria, \q and Benjamin will possess Gilead.
en.R: People from the Negev desert in the south will take over Mount Esau. People from the western foothills will take over the land of the Philistines. \q They will take over the land of Ephraim \q and the land of Samaria. \q The people of Benjamin will take over Gilead.

es.L: Y [los del] Néguev poseerán el monte de Esaú, y [los de] la Sefela a los filisteos; \q y poseerán el territorio de Efraín \q y el territorio de Samaria, \q y Benjamín [poseerá] Galaad.
es.B: La gente del Néguev tomará posesión del monte de Esaú, y la gente de la Sefela, de la tierra de los filisteos; \q tomarán posesión del territorio de Efraín \q y del territorio de Samaria, \q y Benjamín poseerá Galaad.
es.R: La gente del desierto del Néguev, en el sur, se apoderará del monte de Esaú. La gente de las colinas del oeste se apoderará de la tierra de los filisteos. \q Se apoderarán de la tierra de Efraín \q y de la tierra de Samaria. \q La gente de Benjamín se apoderará de Galaad.

fr.L: Et [ceux du] Néguev posséderont la montagne d’Ésaü, et [ceux de] la Shéfela les Philistins ; \q et ils posséderont le territoire d’Éphraïm \q et le territoire de Samarie, \q et Benjamin [possédera] Galaad.
fr.B: Les gens du Néguev prendront possession de la montagne d’Ésaü, et les gens de la Shéfela du pays des Philistins ; \q ils prendront possession du territoire d’Éphraïm \q et du territoire de Samarie, \q et Benjamin possédera Galaad.
fr.R: Les gens du désert du Néguev, au sud, s’empareront de la montagne d’Ésaü. Les gens des collines de l’ouest s’empareront du pays des Philistins. \q Ils s’empareront du pays d’Éphraïm \q et du pays de Samarie. \q Les gens de Benjamin s’empareront de Galaad.

sw.L: Na [wale wa] Negebu watamiliki mlima wa Esau, na [wale wa] Shefela Wafilisti; \q nao watamiliki nchi ya Efraimu \q na nchi ya Samaria, \q na Benyamini [atamiliki] Gileadi.
sw.B: Watu wa Negebu watamiliki mlima wa Esau, na watu wa Shefela nchi ya Wafilisti; \q watamiliki eneo la Efraimu \q na eneo la Samaria, \q naye Benyamini atamiliki Gileadi.
sw.R: Watu wa jangwa la Negebu upande wa kusini watautwaa mlima wa Esau. Watu wa vilima vya magharibi wataitwaa nchi ya Wafilisti. \q Wataitwaa nchi ya Efraimu \q na nchi ya Samaria. \q Watu wa Benyamini wataitwaa Gileadi.

vi.L: Và [người] Nê-ghép sẽ chiếm hữu núi Ê-sau, và [người] Sơ-phê-la [chiếm hữu] người Phi-li-tin; \q và họ sẽ chiếm hữu đồng ruộng Ép-ra-im \q và đồng ruộng Sa-ma-ri, \q và Bên-gia-min [sẽ chiếm hữu] Ga-la-át.
vi.B: Dân miền Nê-ghép sẽ chiếm hữu núi Ê-sau, và dân miền Sơ-phê-la sẽ chiếm đất của người Phi-li-tin; \q họ sẽ chiếm hữu lãnh thổ Ép-ra-im \q và lãnh thổ Sa-ma-ri, \q còn Bên-gia-min sẽ chiếm hữu Ga-la-át.

ko.L: 그리고 네겝 [사람들이] 에서의 산을 차지하고, 세펠라 [사람들이] 블레셋 사람들을 [차지할 것이다]. \q 또 그들이 에브라임의 들판과 \q 사마리아의 들판을 차지하고, \q 베냐민은 길르앗을 [차지할 것이다].

decisions.choice: those of the Negev will possess Mount Esau: each region of Judah takes the land beside it
alternatives: they will possess the Negev and Mount Esau, the Shephelah and the Philistines
decisions.reason: The Hebrew is brief. "The Negev" and "the Shephelah" have no marker of the object, while "Mount Esau" and "the Philistines" do, so the first of each pair is taken as the people who will possess the second: the people of the Negev, Judah's southern desert, take Edom's mountains to the south-east, and the people of the Shephelah, the low hills to the west, take the Philistine plain. Read the other way, "they", the house of Jacob of verse 18, take all four. The picture is the same: the land is restored and enlarged on every side.

decisions.choice: Ephraim, Samaria, Benjamin and Gilead: the lands of the north and east
decisions.reason: Ephraim and Samaria were the heart of the northern kingdom, lost to Assyria in 722 BC. Benjamin lay just north of Jerusalem, and Gilead was Israel's land east of the Jordan. The verse pictures the whole land of Israel restored to its people.

en.L: And the exiles of this host of the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel [will possess] what [belongs to] the Canaanites as far as Zarephath; \q and the exiles of Jerusalem who [are] in Sepharad \q will take possession of the cities of the Negev.

en.R: This large group of Israel's people who were taken away as prisoners will take over the land of the Canaanites as far as Zarephath. \q And the people from Jerusalem who were taken away to Sepharad \q will take over the towns of the Negev.

decisions.choice: the exiles of Israel will possess the land of the Canaanites as far as Zarephath
alternatives: the exiles of Israel who are among the Canaanites as far as Zarephath, together with the exiles of Jerusalem, will possess the cities of the Negev
decisions.reason: This is the hardest verse in the book. It reads word for word "and the exiles of this host of the sons of Israel which Canaanites as far as Zarephath". It is taken here as a clause whose verb, "will possess", is understood from the end of the verse: the exiles of the north take the coast as far as Zarephath, and the exiles of Jerusalem take the Negev. It can also be read as one long subject, the exiles living among the Canaanites, so that both groups of exiles return to the cities of the Negev. "Host" may mean an army or a large company; some take it as a fortress or as a place name.

decisions.choice: the Canaanites as far as Zarephath: the Phoenician coast to the north
decisions.reason: Zarephath was a town on the coast between Tyre and Sidon, where Elijah stayed with a widow (1 Kings 17:9). "Canaanites" here means the Phoenicians of that coast.

decisions.choice: Sepharad: a place of exile not known for certain
alternatives: a place in Media or elsewhere in the east
decisions.reason: Sepharad is named only here. It is often identified with Sardis, the capital of Lydia in Asia Minor, whose name is written in a similar way in old inscriptions; others suggest places in the east. Later Jewish tradition took it to mean Spain, and the Jews of Spain and their descendants are still called Sephardim from this verse. The text says only that some of Jerusalem's exiles were there.

decisions.reason: Literal brackets the words that the reading in m1 supplies; Balanced states them. Readable explains "exiles" as people taken away as prisoners and gives "host" as a large group, without choosing between army and company.

ko.L: 그리고 구원자들이 시온산에 올라가서 \q 에서의 산을 심판할 것이며, \q 왕권은 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께 속할 것이다.
ko.B: 구원자들이 시온산에 올라가 \q 에서의 산을 다스릴 것이고, \q 나라는 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께 속할 것이다.
ko.R: 하나님의 백성을 구해 낼 지도자들이 시온산에 올라가 \q 에서의 산을 다스릴 것이다. \q 그리고 나라는 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 것이 될 것이다.

decisions.choice: deliverers: leaders who save the people, like the judges
decisions.reason: The word is used of the leaders God raised up in the book of Judges to rescue Israel (Judges 3:9, 15; Nehemiah 9:27). The Greek translation reads it with other vowels as "those who have been delivered", the rescued people themselves. The Hebrew text is followed. This description of the Greek is written from general knowledge.

decisions.choice: to judge: to rule and to bring justice
decisions.reason: The verb means to judge, and so to govern, as the judges of Israel did. Mount Esau, which looked down on Jerusalem (verse 3), will be ruled from Mount Zion. The two mountains frame the end of the book.

decisions.choice: the kingship will belong to the LORD: the book's last word
decisions.reason: The book ends not with Israel's victory but with the LORD's reign. The deliverers rule under him, and the kingdom is his (Psalm 22:29; Zechariah 14:9).

decisions.choice: deliverers (L, B); leaders who rescue God's people (R); judge (L); rule over (B, R); kingship (L); kingdom (B, R)
decisions.reason: Readable explains "deliverers" (m1). Balanced and Readable say "rule over" for the sense of "judge" here (m2), and "kingdom" for the reign that belongs to the LORD.
